articles.headline: Letter from Camden, N.J.
articles.author: B
articles.summary: Letter from Camden, N.J., signed 'B.', dated November 29th, 1865 (page 1, columns 2-3). Camden church news; no officers or full names legible enough to link.

articles.headline: Car Question Settled in Cincinnati (editorial note and report)
articles.summary: We give place this week to a righteous decision given by Judge Storer, in favor of a colored man, $800. Colored people can now ride in any car they choose, just as Philadelphia rail companies will have yet to come to, and it would be much better for them to come to it at once than to be driven by law. Report of Isaac Young vs. the Passenger Street Railroad Company (Cincinnati) follows, continued on page 2, column 1 (jury verdict $800).

articles.headline: Notice: Boling and Houston no longer employed by the Book Concern
articles.summary: Our two young friends, Thomas H. Boling and C. J. Houston, are no longer in the employ of the A. M. E. Book Concern. May success attend them in the business they propose to carry on. ED.
people: former employee, A. M. E. Book Concern (619 Pine St.)
former employee, A. M. E. Book Concern (619 Pine St.)

articles.headline: Warning (false agents of the Recorder)
articles.summary: Unknown persons, pretending to be agents for this paper, are sneaking around this city collecting money; one went into an eating saloon and collected money for an advertisement. No names given.

articles.headline: A Grand Location for our Book Concern (standing appeal)
articles.summary: Standing appeal (Nov 4-1mo): a house and lot has been bargained for the A. M. E. Book Concern; $1500 is wanted. Elisha Weaver, Box 2975 / 619 Pine Street.

articles.headline: Letter from Camp Cadwalader
articles.author: Jacob S. Johnson
articles.summary: By special request we publish the following letter for its own merit: Camp Cadwalader, Phila., Pa., December 2d, 1865. Mr. Editor: Allow me, through the medium of your valuable sheet, to return my heartfelt thanks to the officers of the 25th United States Colored Infantry, for the kindness they extended to me, while a member of Co. H. Thanks Colonel F. L. Hitchcock, Lieut. Col. J. W. H. Reisinger, Captain A. A. Shattuck (Co. H) and the regiment's chaplain (unnamed), 'to correct certain erroneous reports that have been circulated.'

articles.headline: Gone Up Another Step (Banneker delegates admitted to the Literary Societies' convention)
articles.summary: The Literary Societies of Philadelphia met in convention on Monday night, the 4th inst., to which colored delegates, from the Banneker Association, were duly accredited. After a powerful address from our esteemed friend, Mr. O. V. Cato, one of the teachers of the High School for colored youth, they were admitted to seats in the Society. Onward still, moves the world.
people: teacher, High School for colored youth (Institute for Colored Youth); speaker

articles.headline: Notice: Ladies' Fair of Wesley Church, Hirst Street (date corrected)
articles.summary: The Ladies' Fair of Wesley Church, Hirst Street, of which Rev. Jacob Mitchell is pastor, will commence on the 13th of December, and not on the 13th of November, as published in our paper last week.

articles.headline: Colored troops' bounty (Military and Naval Agency notice)
articles.summary: The colored troops are all entitled to bounty ... immediate application should be made, either in person or by letter, to the Military and Naval Agency, No. 427 Walnut street, Philadelphia, Joseph E. Devitt & Co. All advice given free of charge. (Agency not known to be Black-run; not linked.)

articles.headline: Letter from Morristown, N.J.: Dedication of Bethel Church
articles.author: W. H. W. Winder
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: After a long silence I again essay to write a few lines for your valuable paper ... After being transferred from the Philadelphia District to the New York District, I received an appointment, in June last, from Bishop A. W. Wayman, to the Morristown station. The church was enlarged by colored carpenters (Gabriel McGill of Stanhope, N.J., his son Henry A. McGill, and John A. Solomon; a well dug by James F. Hoy) and dedicated on Sabbath, November 26th, by the Rev. Wm. Moore, of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, who organized the society over twenty years ago; Rev. Joseph Benedict assisted; Brother Henry Ader welcomed them. Dated Morristown, N.J., Dec. 4, 1865.
people: pastor, Bethel Church, Philadelphia (Rev.); dedicated the church

articles.headline: The Amateur's Companion, by Wm. H. Davis
articles.summary: Mr. Wm. H. Davis, Professor of Music, and late Band-Master of the 22d Reg't United States Colored Troops, has made arrangements to have a musical book published, called the 'Amateur's Companion,' of which he is the author ... The first number will make its appearance on or about December 16th, 1865. Price per copy 50 cents.
people: Professor of Music; late Band-Master, 22d U.S. Colored Troops; author of 'Amateur's Companion' (residence not stated)

articles.headline: A Surprise (St. Thomas' Church Parsonage)
articles.author: W. J. & Annie C. Alston
articles.summary: On the evening of the 30th ult., at about half past eight o'clock, there was a gentle ring at the door-bell of St. Thomas' Church Parsonage, which we hastened to answer, and were greeted with a dozen or more smiling countenances, who were ushered into the parlor, each bearing a basket or attractive package. A purse of twenty-five dollars was placed in Mrs. Alston's hand. 'We cannot refrain from revealing that of the leader of them, viz: Mrs. James H. George.' Philadelphia, Dec. 4th, 1865.

articles.headline: An Appeal: Ladies' Union Sewing Circle of Wesley Church fair
articles.author: Jacob Mitchell
articles.summary: The Ladies' Union Sewing Circle of the A. M. E. Wesley Church, in Hurst street, intend holding a Fair for the benefit of their church, to help to free it from its present embarrassment. Contributions can be sent to the places listed (see event). The fair will commence on Wednesday, the 13th of December, and continue throughout the holidays. Season tickets 25 cts., single 10 cts. Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Elder in charge.
people: receiver of contributions, No. 2 McKee's [VERIFY] Avenue, below Lombard (Mrs.)
receiver of contributions, No. 418 Gaskill St. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Notice: welcome-home sermon to the returned colored soldiers at Bethel
articles.summary: A welcome home and congratulating sermon will be delivered to the returned colored soldiers, on Sunday afternoon, December 10, 1865, at half-past two o'clock, at Bethel Church, Sixth street, above Lombard, by the pastor, Rev. Wm. Moore, assisted by other ministers, to which all returned colored soldiers are earnestly invited.

articles.headline: Special Notice: Bishop Wayman's appointments
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: Bishop Wayman's appointments: Sunday, Dec. 10th, Norfolk and Portsmouth, Virginia ... Monday morning, Dec. 18th, meeting of the Bishops in Philadelphia, at 11 o'clock. Monday night, Dec. 18th, Germantown, Pa. Tuesday night, Dec. 19th, Freehold, N.J. Wednesday night, Dec. 20th, Manalapan, N.J. Thursday night, Dec. 21st, Mt. Holly, N.J.

articles.headline: Semi-centenary of the A. M. E. Church: corresponding committees
articles.author: A. W. W.
articles.summary: The attention of the ministers of the several Annual Conferences has been called to the action of the last Baltimore Annual Conference, respecting the holding of the Semi-centenary anniversary of the A. M. E. Church; and as the committee appointed by the Baltimore Conference have failed to correspond with the Philadelphia and New York Conferences, I would therefore announce the following committees to be corresponded with: Philadelphia Conference: Rev. Wm. Moore, Stephen Smith and Elisha Weaver. New York Conference: Revs. Henry Davis, J. M. Williams and Joshua Woodlyn.

articles.headline: Acknowledgment (donations for the freedmen)
articles.author: Sallie L. Daffin
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Please insert in the columns of your widely circulated paper, the receipt of the following donations for the benefit of the freedmen. Dr. W. Longfellow, $1.00; Mr. W. H. Stokely, 1.00; Mrs. Mary Fields, 1.00; pupils of Wilmington, Del., schools (Miss M. Gertrude Offit's, Mr. Frisby J. Cooper's, Miss Estellina Johnson's); total $14.98. Also clothing from Mrs. Dr. Harris and Mesdames S. Bostick, Diana, Henry and another; books from Mr. Geo. Garnett.

articles.headline: Notice: Professor Jacob A. Raymond's lecture at the Philadelphia Institute
articles.summary: Professor Jacob A. Raymond will deliver a lecture on 'The African Race, and their sure plan of elevation,' at the Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St. above Seventh, on Thursday evening, the 14th instant, under the auspices of the Central Library Company ... Admission 25 cents. The Delmonico Brass Band will be in attendance.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: On the 30th of November, by the Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Mr. Richard Ross to Miss Priscilla Batchelder, both of Philadelphia. ... On Wednesday, the 1st of November, at St. Thomas' Protestant Episcopal Church, by the Rev. W. J. Alston, Mr. Andrew F. Stevens to Miss Isabel L. Cole, both of Philadelphia. ... On the 6th [VERIFY] of November, by Rev. Bishop Wayman, Mr. Jonathan Bovard [VERIFY] to Mrs. Hannah Stout, both of Philadelphia. On Nov. 30th, by Rev. R. P. Gibbs, Mr. John Jacobs, of Delaware, to Miss Rebecca Smith, of Philadelphia. (Also: James Harris to Jane Oliver of Oxford, Pa., and George Anderson to Mary A. Jay of Cecil, Md., both by Rev. John W. Stevenson; William Cooper to Ada Foster of New Haven, Conn., by Rev. William W. Grimes.)
people: officiating minister, St. Thomas' P. E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: U.S. Agency for Colored Soldiers and Seamen (Thomas S. Malcolm, agent)
articles.summary: U. S. Agency for Colored Soldiers and Seamen. Branch Agencies, No. 609 [VERIFY] Walnut St., and 717 Lombard St., Philadelphia, Pa., Thomas S. Malcolm, Agent. General Office, No. 402 N. Y. Avenue, between 13th and 14th Streets, Washington, D.C. Soldiers and seamen can have their claims made out ... C. Leonard, Late Chaplain U.S.A. (Dec 2-2mo).
people: agent, U.S. Agency for Colored Soldiers and Seamen, branch at 717 Lombard St.

articles.headline: S. Shorter Hawkins: New Fall and Winter Dry Goods (615 Lombard)
articles.summary: New Fall and Winter Dry Goods. All the latest styles of merinos, alpacas, poplins, delaines ... colored and white flannels, balmorals and hoop-skirts ... gentlemen's furnishing goods. Call and see at the old stand, S. Shorter Hawkins, 615 Lombard Street, Philada. ('to Apl 1-6m'; the 1865 fall and winter wording.)

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers' and Seamen's U.S. Government Claim Office (John J. Keefe, Jr.)
articles.summary: Colored Soldiers' and Seamen's U. S. Government Claim Office. John J. Keefe, Jr., Attorney, No. 511 S. Sixth St., (below Lombard,) Philadelphia. Soldiers' and seamen's claims for U.S. bounty, State and City bounty, pensions, back pay, prize money ... promptly recovered. Pensions can be obtained ... in one-half the time, at this office, that it will take those who put their claims into the white agencies for collection. (Oct 28-3mos)
people: attorney, claim office, No. 511 S. Sixth St. below Lombard

articles.headline: Joseph H. Cole, Continental Eating Saloon (418 South Sixth, opposite Bethel)
articles.summary: Joseph H. Cole, Continental Eating Saloon, No. 418 South Sixth St., Philadelphia, (Opposite Bethel Church.) Where he continues to keep always on hand the very best assortment of oysters and other refreshments ... Meals served at all hours ... Also, public and private waiting done on the most reasonable terms.
people: proprietor, Continental Eating Saloon, No. 418 South Sixth St., opposite Bethel Church; also public and private waiting

articles.headline: James W. Brown, Steam-Dyeing, Scouring and Repairing Works (S. Fifth above Walnut; Shippen St.)
articles.summary: If you wish your clothing made to look equal to new, go to the Old Established Steam-Dyeing, Scouring, and Repairing Works, No. 139 [VERIFY] S. Fifth St., above Walnut, and No. 1003 [VERIFY] Shippen St., Philadelphia, Pa. James W. Brown. (Formerly with Granville Stokes, No. 606 Chestnut St.)
people: proprietor, steam-dyeing works, S. Fifth St. above Walnut and Shippen St.

articles.headline: The A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Philada.: first Sabbath offering to liquidate the debt
articles.author: Jacob Mitchell
articles.summary: The members and friends of the A. M. E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, propose on the 7th day of January, 1866, being the first Sabbath in the New Year, throughout the entire day, to give to the church, to liquidate the debt on the building, a portion of the first week's earnings of their labor. The debt is thirteen hundred dollars. Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Elder in charge; John H. Hughes, Steward.
people: elder in charge, Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst St. (Rev.)
steward, Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst St.

articles.headline: Appeal of the Trustees of the African Methodist Episcopal Book Concern, of Philadelphia (purchase of No. 631 Pine Street)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: To the Bishops and Ministers of the several Districts of the African Methodist Episcopal Church of America: Dear Brethren: It affords us pleasure to inform you, that after nearly fifty years of the organization of our beloved Church, we have at last succeeded in purchasing a house and lot, in a good location, for our Book Concern and paper, No. 631 Pine street, Philadelphia, not far from where we are now doing business. We have borrowed money to make the first payment, and will get possession on the first of March, 1866. Brethren, we want the sum of $4,000 by the 25th of April, 1866 ...

articles.headline: At Church Last Sabbath (Wesley and Bethel, Dec. 10; returned soldiers; Bethel choir)
articles.summary: On last Sabbath morning we attended divine service at Wesley Church, of which Rev. Jacob Mitchell is pastor, and heard our young brother from California, Rev. John Jenifer. ... At three o'clock we attended Bethel Church to hear Elder Moore's address to the returned soldiers. The church was crowded to its utmost capacity, both up and down stairs. ... After he had concluded, Rev. Jacob Mitchell followed in an exhortation. ... We never heard Bethel choir perform so well as they did on this occasion.
people: pastor, Wesley Church (Rev.); exhorter at Bethel
Elder Moore, pastor of Bethel; address to the returned soldiers

articles.headline: Death of Mrs. Julia C. Collins
articles.summary: We are sorry to inform our readers that we have received a letter from Mr. S. C. Collins, informing us of the death of his estimable wife, Mrs. Julia C. Collins, authoress of 'The Curse of Caste; or, the Slave Bride.' She departed this life on the 25th of November last, and, as the letter says, in the full triumph of everlasting bliss. ... deprived of the pleasure of reading the balance of the beautiful story which she was writing for our paper.

articles.headline: Bishop's Council
articles.summary: On Monday, the 18th, our Bishops will meet, in this city. We anticipate a good time. This is as it ought to be and we hope that they will all meet, if life and health will permit them.

articles.headline: A Letter from Harrisburg (arrest of two discharged colored soldiers)
articles.author: James Robison; James W. Loney
articles.summary: On Thursday afternoon, December 5th, James Robinson, of the Third Regiment, who has just been discharged like myself, was walking along the street, when a small boy, about nine years old, came up and insulted us. Mr. Robinson said to him, 'Go home, you young scamp.' Just then came several officers of the city, and we were arrested and put in the lock-up. We were treated very badly ... Mr. Barrmot [VERIFY], the chief of Police, said to me, 'You are insulted, are you? Who are you to be insulted? You are nothing but a nigger.' ... 'What's your name, sir?' 'James W. Loney.' 'Where are you from, sir?' 'Philadelphia.' Harrisburg, Dec. 5th, 1865.
people: discharged colored soldier, of Philadelphia; arrested at Harrisburg; co-signer

articles.headline: Notice: Third Quarterly Meeting, Zion A. M. E. Mission Church, Seventh Street
articles.author: H. J. Rhodes
articles.summary: The Third Quarterly meeting of the Zion A. M. E. Mission church, Seventh Street, between Dickerson and Tasker streets, will be held on Sunday, Dec. the 24th, 1865, at which time we expect to have present the Revs. W. Moore, E. Weaver, R. P. Gibbs, J. Mitchell, G. E. Boyer, D. P. Seaton, and others. H. J. Rhodes, Minister in charge.

articles.headline: Wm. H. Davis's 'Amateur's Companion' (No. 436 Lyod St.)
articles.author: William H. Davis
articles.summary: The Great Cure. The only way I see that you can be cured [is by] taking Dr. Strickling's Balsam, or Prof. Wm. H. Davis' Amateur's Companion, a new musical work just published at No. 436 Lyod st., Phila. ... 'The Freedman's Polka,' and the splendid ballad ... the five pieces all for fifty cents. Agents wanted in city and country to sell the Amateur's Companion. Those wishing to become subscribers would do well to leave their names and residence at No. 436 Lyod st.
people: Professor of music; publisher of the 'Amateur's Companion', No. 436 Lyod St. (as printed; probably Lloyd St.)

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: In this city, Dec. 2d, by the Rev. T. D. Miller, Mr. Wm. H. Hake, of Augusta, Ga., to Miss Emma C. Belcher, of South Carolina. On Dec. 6th, by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Mr. John Purnell, to Miss Henrietta Figeot, both of this city. On Dec. 7th, by the same, Mr. Thomas Scott, of Richmond, Va., to Mrs. Sophia Howard, of Baltimore, Md. ... On Dec. 7th, by Rev. William Moore, Mr. Joshua B. Anderson, of Kent county, Md., to Miss Letitia C. Miller, of Phila. Anglo-African please copy. On Dec. 10th, by the same, Mr. Elias Tanner, of South Carolina, to Miss Isabella L. Galloway, of Philadelphia. In Kingsessing, Pa., on the 5th inst., by the Rev. Wm. J. Alston, Robert B. Milton, of Indiana, late Sergt. of Co. A, 5th Ohio, to Carder [VERIFY] E., daughter of Rev. Robert Morris, and granddaughter of the late Joshua Jones, of Charleston, S. C.

articles.headline: Prospects of the Colored Race: A Few Stray Thoughts
articles.author: Nicodemus
articles.summary: Signed 'Nicodemus', Philada., Dec. 10th, 1865. The writer met colored soldiers on a New York boat and reports that on the transport from Fortress Monroe to Philadelphia the troops were compelled to occupy the place where cattle had been quartered, and several died on the way; reflections on the franchise. No names given.

articles.headline: Letter from Wilmington, Del.: concert by a Philadelphia company (conclusion)
articles.author: D. P. Seaton
articles.summary: (Begun on p. 1, col. 7, 'The Ball is Still Moving.') Our citizens immediately commenced to prepare for the concert, and at the hour of six o'clock they commenced to stream towards the appointed place ... Black and white, rich and poor, old and young, met together on this occasion ... The concert was conducted splendidly ... Mrs. Merthe Collins acted as leader upon the occasion, and too much credit cannot be awarded her and her able assistants. ... I failed to get their names ... We realized nearly $100 from the concert. Wilmington, Delaware.
people: leader of the Philadelphia concert company (Mrs.; printed 'Merthe', probably Martha)

articles.headline: Personal (Bishops Payne, Wayman and Campbell in the city)
articles.summary: Rev. Bishops Payne, Wayman and Campbell are all in the city. We pray that God will pour out his blessing upon them ... Rev. R. L. Perry, general agent and superintendent of the African Civilization Society of New York, is also in the city.

articles.headline: Camden, New Jersey (quarterly meeting in Brother Boyer's charge)
articles.summary: Last Sunday, upon the invitation of Brother Boyer, we attended the quarterly meeting in his charge. We were highly pleased to learn that the very best feeling exists between pastor and congregation, and that their prospects for the future are bright and hopeful.

articles.headline: 1000 Cash Subscribers for Philadelphia: an appeal to the Citizens of Philadelphia in behalf of this paper
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: Fellow Citizens and friends of the oppressed: one more issue after this will settle the question as to whether this paper, for five years, has been efficiently carried on by your humble servant. ... We want one thousand CASH Subscribers in Philadelphia by the first or tenth of January, 1866. ... As soon as we can get into our new building ... we intend to commence to teach our young men the printing business. The prejudices of the owners of printing establishments have been so great, that no colored men were allowed to learn the art of printing. ... We hope all the class-leaders of our Church in this city will take hold of this matter.

articles.headline: Congratulatory Address of Rev. John E. Price, President of the Garnet Equal Rights League
articles.author: Alex. T. Harris
articles.summary: Congratulatory Address of the Rev. John E. Price, President of the 'Garnet Equal Rights League,' delivered on the evening of the 6th [VERIFY] of December, 1865. Ladies and Gentlemen of the Garnet League: A little less than four months ago, you met together, and under the most discouraging circumstances organized this League. ... you have grown from a handful to the number of two hundred and twenty members; comprising some of the most wealthy, intelligent and respectable citizens of this city ... In point of numbers, you are now the Banner League of the old Keystone State. (Continued on p. 3, col. 1, and signed there 'Alex. T. Harris'.) The Garnet League is the HARRISBURG auxiliary (see the Dec 30 'Letter from Harrisburg'), so no names are linked.

articles.headline: Wm. H. Davis's 'Amateur's Companion' (notice, 436 Lynd St.)
articles.author: Wm. H. Davis
articles.summary: A Contribution to American History. The life and times of Joseph Warren, by Richard Frothingham ... together with the Amateur's Companion, published at No. 436 Lynd St., Phila. The Amateur's Companion has met with great success, at 436 Lynd St., Phila. ... Agents wanted in the city and country ... leave their names and residence at 436 Lyod St., Phila. Office hours from 9 A.M. to 1 P.M. (Repeat in substance of the Dec 16 notice, entered there.)

articles.headline: Situation wanted (barber from Richmond; inquire at 619 Pine)
articles.summary: There is a very nice young man from Richmond, Va., who is a barber by trade, and is now out of employment. He can also act as a waiter. You can learn something about him by inquiring at No. 619 Pine St., Phila.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: On Dec. 18th, by Rev. R. P. Gibbs, Mr. Wm. H. Boyer to Miss Anna Land, all of Phila. (Also: John A. Jemas [?] of Norfolk to Eliza Jane Craig, Alexandria, Va.; Alfred Cabbage to Rachel E. Vionay, Kent Co., Del., by Rev. G. T. Waters; Benjamin Thomas of Montgomery County to Angeline Wilhelm of Schuylkill County, Pa., by Rev. Mr. Porter.)

articles.headline: Obituary: Priscilla L. Bedford, of Frankford
articles.summary: Died, at Frankford, Pa., on Thursday the 7th inst., after a lingering illness, Priscilla L., wife of Moses [VERIFY] Bedford, aged 25 years, 11 months, and 4 weeks.

articles.headline: Missionary Circular of the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society of the A.M.E. Church
articles.author: Daniel A. Payne
articles.summary: Mission Rooms, No. 10 Saratoga St., Baltimore, Dec. 13, '65. Circular to the ministers of the A.M.E. Church: $10,000 apportioned among the districts (Philadelphia District $1,500); the only responses so far are the Philadelphia Conference, $250, and Indiana, $69. Officers: President, Bishop Daniel A. Payne; Vice-Presidents, Bishops Wm. P. Quinn, A. W. Wayman, J. P. Campbell; Executive Committee: Daniel W. Moore, S. L. Hammonds, George T. Watkins, J. H. S. Hall, William D. W. Schureman, John J. Herbert; Treasurer, Jas. H. Davis. (Baltimore-based; continued on p. 2.)

articles.headline: A Jolly Time in Philadelphia (church fairs)
articles.summary: The most of our people are having a jolly time in our city, in holding fairs and festivals. Wesley Church, Hurst St., of which Rev. Jacob Mitchell is pastor, has been holding a fair for over a week, and the house has been greatly crowded. The ladies of St. Thomas' Church, of which Rev. Mr. Alston is pastor, have also been at work for several nights. Wesley Church, Lombard St., of which Rev. Mr. Hemer is pastor, is also holding a fair in their church. Little Pine, or Minster St. Baptist Church, has been, and is still holding a fair, and doing very well. Union Bethel Church, of which Rev. J. P. Gibbs is pastor, is also holding a fair for organ for church. Hence, you see we are having a gay time in the city of Brotherly Love.
people: pastor, Union Bethel Church (Rev.; printed J. P.)

articles.headline: The Closing Number of Volume Fifth, 1865
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: The present number completes the Fifth Volume of the Christian Recorder, which commenced its career on the first day of January, 1860, making full five years since we assumed the management of so great a cause as that in which we are now engaged. ... remains a mystery to our own mind how we have regularly issued the paper, beside the superintendence of our Book Depository, the publishing of Hymn-books, Disciplines, Love-feast tickets, &c. Signed 'The Editor'.

articles.headline: Meeting of the Colored Citizens of Philadelphia (Dec. 21)
articles.author: J. B. Young
articles.summary: An adjourned public meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia was held in the Philadelphia Institute, on Thursday evening, December 21st, 1865. Richard H. Gleaves, president, in the chair. This meeting being a third of the series of well-attended, enthusiastic public gatherings held weekly in the same place. The meeting was opened with prayer by the Rev. Stephen Smith. The minutes of the last meeting were read by the Secretary, Mr. J. B. Young, and approved.
people: opened with prayer; spoke; publication committee (Rev.)
committee on the Chambers sermon (printed 'D. Bassett'); addressee of Sumner's letter; publication committee
mover; committee to the Social, Civil and Statistical Association
committee to the Social, Civil and Statistical Association

articles.headline: Letter from Peekskill (the Philadelphia Tent and the Sarah Tent of New York)
articles.author: Elizabeth Doffels
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I take pleasure in informing you that I noticed in the Christian Recorder, a few weeks ago, an article which drew my attention, in regard to the separation of the Philadelphia Tent from the Sarah Tent of New York. It is doubtful to me if they were ever united. I was surprised when I heard of them declaring their independence, on account of the neglect of Sister Martha Tow. ... Philadelphia sent five delegates to the city of New York, on July 1st, 1864 ... to confer the degrees upon Rebecca Tent, of Philadelphia; but, as yet, they have never sent for me. Elizabeth Doffels (printed also 'Duffels'), M. of M. J. D. J. U., Peekskill, West Chester Co., New York.

articles.headline: Appointment: Rev. A. C. Crippin as Travelling Book Agent
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference, at its last Session, passed a resolution requesting the Presiding Bishop to appoint a travelling Book Agent, as provided for in the Discipline, page 283. For reasons not necessary now to give, the appointment has not been made sooner. We have, therefore, appointed Rev. A. C. Crippin as the Travelling Book Agent of the African Methodist Episcopal Church. A. W. Wayman. Phila., Dec. 21, 1865.
people: Travelling Book Agent of the A.M.E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Notice: special discourse at the Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, 7th Street
articles.author: H. J. Rhodes
articles.summary: There will be a special discourse delivered at the Zion A. M. E. Mission Church, 7th Street, between Dickerson and Tasker Sts., on Sunday, December 31st, 1865, at 3 o'clock, P.M., Providence permitting. The subject will be 'The Sign of the Times,' by H. J. Rhodes, Pastor.
people: pastor, Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, 7th St. (printed RHODES in small caps)

articles.headline: Meeting of the E. R. League of Bensalem
articles.author: James Fillman
articles.summary: Mr. Weaver: Dear Sir: A meeting of the E. R. League, of Bensalem, auxiliary to the State E. R. League, was held here on Thursday evening last. We were favored with the presence of Messrs. William D. Forten and Octavius V. Catto, of Philadelphia, whose spirited addresses gave life and interest to the meeting. ... Yours for equal rights, James Fillman, Solicitor. Bensalem, Bucks County, Pa., Dec. 25th, 1865.
people: Solicitor, Bensalem E. R. League (Bucks County)

articles.headline: Wm. H. Davis, Amateur's Companion (436 Lynd Street)
articles.author: Wm. H. Davis
articles.summary: The authorities must take hold and give protection to the citizens. The office of the musical work known as the Amateur's Companion is run down daily by hundreds rushing to purchase copies, and as the mob is becoming greater, I ask protection at No. 436 Lyod Street. ... leave their names and residence at No. 436 Lynd Street, Philadelphia. Office hours from 9 A.M. until 1 P.M. (Puff; entered Dec 16.)

events.name: Literary Societies of Philadelphia, convention: Banneker Association delegates admitted
events.description: The Literary Societies of Philadelphia met in convention on Monday night, December 4, 1865; colored delegates from the Banneker Association were duly accredited and, after an address by Mr. O. V. Cato, a teacher of the High School for colored youth (Institute for Colored Youth), were admitted to seats. No other delegates named.

events.name: Surprise visit and donation, St. Thomas' Church Parsonage
events.description: About 8:30 p.m. on November 30, 1865, a dozen or more parishioners called at St. Thomas' parsonage with baskets of groceries and presented Mrs. Annie C. Alston a purse of twenty-five dollars. The leader is named as Mrs. James H. George; the rest are not named. Reported by W. J. and Annie C. Alston, Dec. 4.

events.name: Ladies' Union Sewing Circle of Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street: fair
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Fair for the benefit of the church, to free it from debt, from Wednesday, December 13, 1865, through the holidays; season tickets 25 cts., single 10 cts. (the p. 2 notice corrects an earlier date of November 13). Contributions to: Rev. Jacob Mitchell, No. 513 [VERIFY] Lombard St. above 5th; Mrs. Lucinda [VERIFY] Waters, No. 218 Currant [VERIFY] Alley above 10th; Mrs. Harriet West, No. 2 McKee's [VERIFY] Avenue below Lombard; Mr. Garroway [VERIFY] Chase, barber shop, Catharine St. above 9th; Mr. William Mullison [VERIFY], [court name illegible] court, first court above 2d St., west of Spruce; Mrs. Jane [VERIFY] Lewis, No. 724 Russell St. between 8th and 9th, Shippen and Fitzwater; Mrs. Ann Hollingsworth, No. 418 Gaskill St.; Mrs. [given name illegible] Queen, No. 514 South 7th St. Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Elder in charge.

events.name: Welcome-home sermon to the returned colored soldiers, Bethel Church
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth street above Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday afternoon, December 10, 1865, 2:30 p.m.: a welcome home and congratulating sermon to the returned colored soldiers by the pastor, Rev. Wm. Moore, assisted by other ministers (not named); all returned colored soldiers invited.

events.name: Meeting of the A.M.E. Bishops in Philadelphia; Bishop Wayman at Germantown
events.description: Per Bishop A. W. Wayman's appointments: Monday morning, December 18, 1865, at 11 o'clock, meeting of the Bishops in Philadelphia; Monday night, December 18, Bishop Wayman at Germantown, Pa.; then Freehold, N.J. (Dec 19), Manalapan, N.J. (Dec 20), Mt. Holly, N.J. (Dec 21).

events.name: Central Library Company: lecture by Professor Jacob A. Raymond
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St. above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: Thursday evening, December 14, 1865: Professor Jacob A. Raymond lectures on 'The African Race, and their sure plan of elevation,' under the auspices of the Central Library Company; admission 25 cents; the Delmonico Brass Band to attend.

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street: New Year's Sabbath debt offering
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Announced for the first Sabbath of 1866 (January 7): members and friends to give a portion of their first week's earnings to liquidate the $1,300 debt on the building. Sermons at 10 1/2 A.M. by Rev. R. P. Gibbs; at 3 P.M. by Revs. Wm. Moore and Stephen Smith; at 7 P.M. by Rev. Bishop Wayman and others. Rev. Jacob Mitchell, Elder in charge; John H. Hughes, Steward.

events.name: A.M.E. Book Concern buys house and lot at No. 631 Pine Street
events.description: The trustees of the A.M.E. Book Concern of Philadelphia announce the purchase of a house and lot at No. 631 Pine Street for the Book Concern and the Recorder (then at 619 Pine). First payment made with borrowed money; possession March 1, 1866; $4,000 wanted by April 25, 1866. The ground fronts on two streets and is valued at $3,000; the building is to train young men in printing and young women in book-binding, paper-folding and bookselling. Committee: Elisha Weaver, chairman; S. Smith; G. M. Mitchell; R. P. Gibbs; W. Moore; H. G. Rhodes. Contributions by Adams' Express or P.O. Box 2075 (elsewhere printed 2975), Philadelphia. (Notice runs dec16 to ap25.)

events.name: Welcome-home address to the returned colored soldiers at Bethel Church (report)
events.location: Bethel Church, Sixth St. above Lombard, Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday, December 10, 1865, 3 p.m.: Elder (Wm.) Moore's address to the returned soldiers; the church was crowded up and down stairs; Rev. Jacob Mitchell followed with an exhortation and the editor (Weaver) spoke to the soldiers at Mitchell's request. The Bethel choir sang, led by Brother Henry Gordoo [VERIFY] (probably Gordon); performers named only as brother Hance[?]... (illegible), sisters Collins and Misses Armstrong. In the morning Rev. John Jenifer, 'our young brother from California', preached at Wesley Church (Rev. Jacob Mitchell, pastor), and in the evening at Bethel. No soldiers or regiments named.

events.name: Arrest of discharged colored soldiers James Robison and James W. Loney by Harrisburg police
events.description: As told in their signed letter dated Harrisburg, Dec. 5th, 1865: James Robison (in the text 'Robinson'), of the Third Regiment, just discharged, and James W. Loney, of Philadelphia, also a discharged soldier, rebuked a boy of about nine who insulted them; city officers arrested both and put them in the lock-up, where they were 'treated very badly'. The chief of police, Mr. Barrmot [VERIFY], told Loney 'You are nothing but a nigger' and 'We don't want your black character proved in Harrisburg.' Next morning they were brought out for examination; the outcome is not stated. Loney asks 'what the black man has been fighting for.' (Police violence and harassment of returned soldiers; not a streetcar case.)

events.name: Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, Seventh Street: Third Quarterly Meeting
events.location: Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, Seventh Street between Dickerson and Tasker streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Third Quarterly meeting, Sunday, December 24, 1865; expected: Revs. W. Moore, E. Weaver, R. P. Gibbs, J. Mitchell, G. E. Boyer, D. P. Seaton and others. H. J. Rhodes, minister in charge.

events.name: Concert by a company of Philadelphia ladies and gentlemen for the A.M.E. Church, Wilmington, Del.
events.description: Thanksgiving Day, December 7, 1865: a concert given by a company of ladies and gentlemen from Philadelphia for the benefit of the A.M.E. Church at Wilmington, reported by its pastor D. P. Seaton (p. 1, col. 7, and p. 2, col. 1). The house was crowded, black and white; Mrs. Merthe [VERIFY] Collins (probably Martha) was leader; nearly $100 realized. The other performers are not named ('I failed to get their names').

events.name: Garnet Equal Rights League (Harrisburg): congratulatory address of its president
events.description: Address by the Rev. John E. Price, President of the Garnet Equal Rights League, delivered on the evening of December 6 [VERIFY: day blurred], 1865, transmitted over the name of Alex. T. Harris. The League was organized a little under four months before (about August 1865) and had 220 members, 'the Banner League of the old Keystone State'. Its record as listed: introduced the reading of essays and pay lectures (25 cts.) in the city; on November 14, 1865 gave 'to the colored soldiers of this State, a reception worthy of their heroic deeds'; defended Wm. Bush, a returned colored soldier, assaulted on the 1?th ult. [day illegible] by a gang of rowdies, beaten and jailed 'because he was a colored man' to await trial before the Court of Quarter Sessions, where the League supplied counsel and won his release and had his assailants held for the next term on a charge of assault with intent to kill; secured from the Public School Board a school in the Fourth Ward. The League met at the Zion church, Harrisburg (Dec 30 issue), so 'this city', the Fourth Ward school and the Court of Quarter Sessions are Harrisburg's (Dauphin County). Price proposes a separate school for girls taught by a competent female teacher paid from League funds, Sabbath-school work and a reading room.

events.name: Assault on Wm. Bush, returned colored soldier, and his jailing (Harrisburg)
events.description: Per the Garnet League address (Dec 23, p. 2): Wm. Bush, a returned colored soldier, was assaulted in November 1865 (the '1?th ult.'; day illegible) by a gang of rowdies, unmercifully beaten, and then thrust into prison 'because he was a colored man', to await trial before the Court of Quarter Sessions. The Garnet Equal Rights League provided counsel and secured his release, and had his assailants prosecuted and held to appear at the next term on a charge of assault with intent to kill. (Mob and police violence at Harrisburg; not a streetcar case. Non-Philadelphia: not linked.)

events.name: Garnet Equal Rights League: reception of the colored soldiers of Pennsylvania at Harrisburg (mentioned)
events.description: Mentioned in the Garnet League address: 'On the 14th of November last, you succeeded in giving to the colored soldiers of this State, a reception worthy of their heroic deeds and undying valor.' No route, marshals, units or speakers given here. This is the Harrisburg reception (grand review) of the colored soldiers of the State; Philadelphia participants, if any, are not named in these issues.

events.name: Bishop Wayman preaches at Wesley Church, Philadelphia (appointment)
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's appointments list ends: 'Sunday Jan. 7th, Wesley Church, Philada., Pa.' (the day of Wesley's New Year debt offering announced Dec 16), after Sullivan St. and First St. churches in New York and Brooklyn, Hudson City, Albany, Coxsackie, Catskill, Morristown N.J. (Jan 4) and Reading, Pa. (Jan 5). He adds that he has visited all the stations and circuits but two in the Philadelphia and New York Conferences.

events.name: Church fairs and festivals in Philadelphia, holiday season 1865
events.description: Per 'A Jolly Time in Philadelphia' (Dec 30): fairs under way in late December 1865 at Wesley Church, Hurst St. (Rev. Jacob Mitchell; over a week, crowded), St. Thomas' Church (the ladies; Rev. Mr. Alston; several nights), Wesley Church, Lombard St. (Rev. Mr. Hemer [VERIFY]), the Little Pine or Minster St. Baptist Church, and Union Bethel Church (Rev. J. P. Gibbs; for an organ).

events.name: Adjourned public meeting of the colored citizens of Philadelphia (third weekly meeting)
events.location: Philadelphia Institute, Lombard St. above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: Thursday evening, December 21, 1865; the third of a series of weekly meetings at the same place. Richard H. Gleaves, president, in the chair; prayer by Rev. Stephen Smith; minutes read by the secretary, J. B. Young. The committee of Messrs. D. [E. D.] Bassett, U. B. Vidal and R. H. Gleaves, appointed at a previous meeting to express the sentiments of the colored community on the Thanksgiving Day sermon of Rev. John Chambers, reported resolutions they had printed and read an Evening Bulletin editorial praising them; report approved, committee discharged. The committee to thank Hon. Charles Sumner and Hon. William D. Kelley made a supplemental report with Sumner's letter (Senate Chamber, Dec. 15, 1865) addressed to E. D. Bassett and Isaiah C. Wear, Esqs.: 'This republic must be free; but this cannot be until all men are equal before the law.' Resolutions moved by U. B. Vidal, discussed by the mover, Rev. Stephen Smith, John C. Bowers [VERIFY; printed 'Bonors'] and J. E. Glasgow, adopted: that the word 'white' be stricken from the statute book; rejoicing that 'slave' is no longer recognized by American laws. On motion of Perry Mitchell: since the 'Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania' had arranged a public demonstration to celebrate the abolition of slavery, a committee of three (Messrs. Mitchell, Vidal and Thos. Charnock) to convey the meeting's approval and willingness to take part. Publication committee: E. D. Bassett, Rev. Stephen Smith, J. B. Young. Adjourned to Wednesday evening, December 27, 1865, same place.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania: planned celebration of the abolition of slavery (announced)
events.description: Reported in the Dec. 21 citizens' meeting: the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania had 'already made arrangements for a public demonstration for the celebration of the abolition of slavery in our country' (the Thirteenth Amendment); the citizens' meeting named Perry Mitchell, U. B. Vidal and Thos. Charnock to convey its approval and willingness to participate. Date, route and marshals not given in this issue.

events.name: Equal Rights League of Bensalem (auxiliary to the State League): meeting with Philadelphia speakers
events.description: Held 'on Thursday evening last' before the letter of Monday, Dec. 25, 1865, i.e. Thursday, December 21 (computed). Addresses by William D. Forten and Octavius V. Catto, of Philadelphia. Reported by James Fillman, Solicitor of the Bensalem League.

events.name: Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, 7th Street: special discourse 'The Sign of the Times'
events.location: Zion A.M.E. Mission Church, 7th Street between Dickerson and Tasker Sts., Philadelphia
events.description: Sunday, December 31, 1865, 3 p.m.: special discourse by the pastor, H. J. Rhodes, on 'The Sign of the Times'.
